stimulus.text: Whereas by an Act made in the last session of Parliament, several duties were granted, continued, and appropriated, toward defraying the expenses of defending, protecting, and securing, the British Colonies and Plantations in America: and whereas it is just and necessary, that Provision be made for raising a further revenue within your Majesty's Dominions in America, toward defraying the said expenses...

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Stamp Act, 1765, preamble (abridged), public domain.

books.section: B. Debt and Taxation Following the French and Indian War
The Sugar Act, the Currency Act, and the Stamp Act

stem: The preamble's phrase 'a further revenue' most directly implies which of the following?

options.text: Parliament had never collected any revenue from the colonies before 1765
options.misconception: 'Further' means additional — Parliament was already collecting duties, as the preamble itself says several duties 'were granted, continued, and appropriated.'

options.text: Parliament was already collecting duties from the colonies and now wanted more
The colonies had asked Parliament to raise additional revenue for their defense
options.misconception: Nothing in the preamble suggests the colonies asked for this — the colonists protested the new duties as soon as they heard of them.

options.text: The new duties would replace all taxes levied by colonial assemblies
options.misconception: The preamble says nothing about replacing assembly taxes — the assemblies kept taxing, which was exactly why colonists called the Stamp Act an invasion of their rights.

rationales.B: 'Further revenue' means more on top of what already existed. The preamble itself says duties 'were granted, continued, and appropriated' — Parliament was already collecting, and now it wanted more.
rationales.A: 'Further' cannot mean 'first.' The word itself says more revenue was being added to revenue already collected.
rationales.C: The colonists never asked for this tax — the preamble is Parliament's claim, not a colonial request.
rationales.D: The assemblies kept their taxing power. The Stamp Act added a parliamentary tax on top of it, which was the colonists' complaint.
rationales.general:
1. Slow down on 'further.' It means additional — more revenue on top of revenue already being collected.
2. Find the proof in the same sentence. The preamble says duties 'were granted, continued, and appropriated' before this act.
3. Ask why the word matters. If Parliament was already taxing the colonies, the fight was not about whether Parliament could tax at all — it was about a new kind of tax, laid directly on the colonists.
Remember: one small word can carry the whole argument — 'further' tells you this tax was an addition, not a beginning.
